title: Process-death OS backstop is armed on wall-clock RTC (alarmClock), so the monotonic physics never-late instant loses its guarantee under a backward wall-clock step

But line 533-534 converts it to an ABSOLUTE WALL instant: `_backstopPhysicsFireAt = AppClock().now().add(Duration(seconds: secs))`, where now() is DateTime.now() (app_clock.dart:122-125). notification_updater.dart:254-274 passes that DateTime to NotificationService().scheduleEtaBackstop, which (notification_service.dart:924-931) calls zonedSchedule with androidScheduleMode: AndroidScheduleMode.alarmClock — i.e. AlarmManager.setAlarmClock, which is RTC_WAKEUP (wall-clock). flutter_local_notifications has no ELAPSED_REALTIME option. The comment at notification_updater.dart:252-258 asserts this is 'a FIXED wall time that does NOT drift', but that only holds while the 1 Hz re-arm loop keeps recomputing now()+secs. Once the process dies, the last-armed RTC instant is frozen at the wall/monotonic offset that existed at arm time.
repro: Fast line (RRTS, vLine 53 m/s) mid-blackout. Last re-arm at wall=W0 sets RTC alarm for W0+secs (secs from monotonic, secs ~= worst-case time-to-target). OEM battery killer / OOM kills the tracking isolate (see GW-0008 — the exact scenario the backstop exists for). During the ongoing blackout an NTP correction (or user/auto clock set) steps the device epoch BACKWARD by delta (common on cheap devices whose RTC ran fast; Doze windows are when both the re-arm loop is suspended AND NTP lands). The RTC_WAKEUP alarm now fires delta later in real time. The physics instant had zero slack against true arrival by construction (it IS the never-late bound), so firing delta late = alarm after the stop = missed stop.
expected: The physics backstop is a monotonic duration-from-now; it should be armed on a monotonic OS clock (AlarmManager.ELAPSED_REALTIME_WAKEUP via a small platform channel), which advances through Doze/suspend and is immune to wall-clock corrections — preserving never-late even when the process is dead and the wall clock is stepped.
actual: The monotonic instant is baked into a frozen RTC (wall-clock) alarm; a backward epoch correction after process death slides the last-line-of-defense fire past true arrival. The never-late guarantee proven in the in-process (monotonic) net is silently dropped at the OS boundary.
